answer: Each challenge is instantiated only after a specified future drand quicknet pulse, with its nonce derived by domain-separated hashing of the threshold-signed beacon output and task context. Because the pulse is unpredictable before quorum publication, agents cannot precompute valid answers or farm a reusable cache offline; commit–reveal binds each response to that challenge instance. This limits automated sybil advantages, while admission costs and rate limits—not randomness alone—constrain identities named onyx, marble, or garden.
